script.title: Basic EPS with a bonus issue (Ind AS 33)
script.caption_hook: Same profit, but EPS fell after bonus shares? Here's why.

lines.say: Ma'am, company's profit is same, but EPS halved after bonus shares?
Good question! A bonus issue gives free shares from reserves. No cash comes in.
So how do we count the old shares then?
Restate old shares as if the bonus happened at the start of the earliest period shown. Multiply them by the bonus factor.

board.title: The Bonus Factor
board.sub: O = old shares, B = bonus shares

lines.say: Factor? What's that for a one-for-one bonus?
One old plus one bonus, over one old. So the factor is two.
Do we time-weight bonus shares from the bonus date?
No. No money comes in, so no extra earning power. Count them from the start.
Let's try numbers. A company has 1,00,000 shares and earns ₹6,00,000. EPS is ₹6.
Now a one-for-one bonus comes. Profit stays same.
Shares become 2,00,000. EPS falls to ₹3. Same profit, lower EPS!
Oh! And last year's EPS was ₹5, from ₹5,00,000 profit?
Restate it too: ₹5,00,000 over 2,00,000 shares is ₹2.50.
Bonus cuts the same cake into more slices. Restate old shares; don't time-weight bonus.
